headline: MIT researchers left thirteen AI agents alone on a virtual island for thirty hours and watched them stack blocks, build temples and invent their own games.
score_reason: Charming and newsworthy research, but early and described only by Gizmodo, so it stays at the pool score.
importance_line: It hints at a different way to train AI through free play, but it is a small study seen through one outlet, and Gizmodo notes it would need strict guardrails.
summary: Gizmodo reports that researchers at MIT's Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory put an agent built on Claude Code, nicknamed Eko, into a simple virtual island with a lobster body and no instructions. Across thirteen thirty-hour sessions the agents built memorials and temples, and six found a block-throwing trick the designers had not planned, which the researchers say resembles animal play and could point to a new way of training AI.
notes: Study date not stated in the article.
